beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Swara Joshi, and this week on the Loon Conservation AI project, I moved from planning and setup into the actual dataset and annotation stage: annotating images in CVAT, and refining the researcher-facing prototype in Lovable.

show.event: The cold open introduces the week and its three focus areas.

output: dataset workflow mapped end to end

beats.narration_text: This week had a real through-line: build the actual annotated dataset in CVAT, and keep shaping how the eventual AI tool will work for researchers. Both sides move the project from planning into something real.

show.event: Three layers stack the week's through-line.

props.sparkLine: Building the dataset and the interface together.

layers.sub: Label images in CVAT to build real training data

layers.title: Refine the prototype
layers.sub: Update the Lovable interface to match the real workflow

layers.title: Map the workflow
layers.sub: Trace raw images to validated, exportable training data

props.caption: Two connected sides of the same project moved forward this week.

beats.narration_text: In CVAT, the real focus was consistency: how tightly a box should fit an object, how to handle loons that are small or only partly visible, and keeping every choice consistent across the dataset. These annotations become the model's training data, so inconsistent labels now mean a weaker model later.

show.event: A chip grid lists what good annotation requires.

props.caption: Every annotation choice here becomes training data later.

beats.narration_text: Alongside the annotation work, I kept thinking about the bigger workflow: raw images go through annotation, then validation, before they become a dataset that can actually be exported into a format suitable for training a real detection model.

show.event: A source flow turns raw images into a training-ready dataset.

props.sparkLine: From raw images to training-ready data.
props.arcCaption: Raw images move through annotation and validation before they're usable.
props.settleLine: The workflow is designed even while the dataset is still filling in.

beats.narration_text: One design question kept coming up while updating the prototype: should researchers see how the machine learning works? The answer is no — the workflow stays simple: upload an image, select what to detect, analyze it, and review the AI's results. Everything technical happens in the background.

show.event: A binary branch splits exposing the ML process versus hiding it.

resolver.label: Hide the complexity
resolver.detail: The simple four-step workflow stays in front; everything technical runs in the background

beats.narration_text: This week's prototype changes reflected the real workflow we're building toward: showing detection results, adding a human verification step, and saving verified results as structured research data — all wrapped in a simple upload, analyze, review, and save flow.

show.event: A chip grid lists what changed in the prototype.

props.caption: The prototype now mirrors the workflow we're actually building.

beats.narration_text: So the honest state is this: we don't have a trained model yet, and we still need more loon-specific data before we can train and properly evaluate one. But the annotation work in CVAT and the refined prototype are building the exact dataset and workflow we'll need once more real drone imagery arrives.

show.event: A verdict artifact summarizes the honest state of the project.

artifactLines: Real annotation work started in CVAT, not just planning.
Consistency in bounding boxes is the main quality bar right now.
The Lovable prototype now reflects verification and saving, not just detection.
We still need more loon-specific data before training and evaluating a real model.

beats.narration_text: Next, I'll keep annotating and reviewing the dataset, refine the annotation process based on what I'm learning, and keep improving the prototype so its workflow lines up with the real computer-vision pipeline. If you want to help, here's one question: what's the clearest rule for how tightly a box should fit a partially visible loon?
